title: PUBLIC NOTICE15th Jul 2026
text: The Commission reminds all voters that taking photographs or recording images of marked ballot papers inside the polling booth is strictly prohibited and constitutes an election offence under Section 7(3)(e) of the Election Offences Act, No. 37 of 2016. Section 7(3)(e) of the Election Offences Act states that a person attending any proceedings relating to an election who, without lawful excuse, captures an image of any marked ballot for purposes of financial gain or for showing allegiance, commits an offence. The offence is punishable by a fine not exceeding KSh 1 million, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years, or both. The Commission urges all voters to comply with this legal requirement in order to protect the secrecy and integrity of the ballot. For accurate and up-to-date information, please visit our official website (https://iebc.or.ke) and follow our verified social media platforms (@IEBCKenya). #16thJulyByElection #YourVoteYourVoice #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

text: The IEBC Electoral Code of Conduct Enforcement Committee, chaired by Commissioner Dr. Alutalala Mukhwana, has found the Member of the National Assembly for Nakuru Town East, Hon. title: Press Release -  Update on Preparedness for the 16th July 2026 Ol Kalou By-Election14th Jul 2026
text: The Commission wishes to inform the nation that all preparations for the by-election scheduled for Thursday, 16th July 2026, to fill the position of Member of National Assembly for Ol Kalou Constituency in Nyandarua County are progressing as planned. All registered voters in Ol Kalou Constituency MUST present their national identity card or valid passport on polling day, as these remain the primary identification documents required for voting. The Register of Voters for the Ol Kalou Constituency by-election remains secure. Claims that the Register has been manipulated are false, misleading and unsupported by evidence. The Commission condemns such misleading claims and urges all stakeholders to refrain from spreading misinformation and disinformation. Polling stations will open at 6:00 a.m. and close at 5:00 p.m. Where polling commences later than scheduled due to unforeseen circumstances, the lost time will be compensated to ensure that voters receive the full polling period. All voters who are in the queue by 5:00 p.m. will be allowed to cast their ballots. Taking photographs or recording images of marked ballot papers inside the polling booth is strictly prohibited and constitutes an election offence under Section 7(3)(e) of the Election Offences Act, No. 37 of 2016. The Commission, in close collaboration with the National Police Service, has put in place adequate security arrangements to ensure a peaceful and orderly electoral process. Two uniformed police officers will be deployed at every polling station, while additional officers will be stationed at tallying centres to maintain law and order and safeguard the integrity of the election. All political parties, candidates, agents and supporters are reminded that compliance with the Electoral Code of Conduct is mandatory. The Commission will not hesitate to invoke all enforcement measures provided for under the Electoral Code of Conduct without fear or favour. The Commission's investigation team is actively investigating all alleged violations with a view to fully enforcing the Code. The Commission calls upon voters, political parties, candidates, observers, civil society organizations and members of the public to report any electoral offence or breach of the Electoral Code of Conduct. Members of the public are encouraged to REPORT and PROVIDE evidence of any electoral malpractice to the Commission, the National Police Service or any other authorized investigative agency. The Commission remains steadfast in its commitment to delivering a peaceful, free, fair, transparent and credible election whose outcome reflects the freely expressed will of the people. Registered voters of Ol Kalou Constituency: Your vote is your voice. Turn out in large numbers, cast your ballot and peacefully shape the future of your constituency. title: IEBC, UNDP Collaborate to Enhance Electoral Integrity and Preparedness for 20279th Jun 2026
text: The Commission, led by Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, today attended a meeting of the local Project Appraisal Committee (LPAC) of the UNDP-led Elections Project document to finalise plans for the Elections Basket Fund project ahead of the 2027 General Election. Speaking during the meeting, Ethekon thanked the development partners, security agencies, gender, youth and women groups present for their support and noted that an election is not a one-day event but a journey where agencies walk together to help achieve an inclusive, transparent, credible, free and fair election. "This collaboration is important for us to build trust and legitimacy of the electoral processes. It is the framework to support elections and a vehicle to mobilise resources for both technical and financial support in the build-up to the 2027 General Election," said Ethekon. The Elections Project document defines the scope, outcomes, outputs and activities required to be implemented prior to the 2027 General Election. If approved and implemented, it will enhance stakeholder engagement and strengthen efforts towards delivering a transparent and credible election. "Election is a journey and I call upon everyone present here today to act responsibly, be accountable for the resources available and work together to achieve tangible results. This document will be taken to the Attorney General and National Treasury for approval before we sign and implement it. I will follow up on the remaining processes to ensure that it is cleared and approved," said Ethekon. Commissioner Ann Nderitu, CBS, said the Elections Project document is anchored on five priorities arising from the 2025 Needs Assessment Mission, including: participation of youth, women and people living with disabilities; strengthening stakeholder engagement and communication; capacity building and technical assistance; electoral security, preparation and early risk awareness coordination; and information integrity to counter misinformation, disinformation and online harm. UNDP’s Resident Representative Jean-Luc Stalon reiterated their support in ensuring the Commission delivers on its constitutional mandate. UNDP has played a pivotal role over successive elections in supporting Kenya to deepen its democracy by contributing to institutional capacity and electoral integrity. LPAC is a mandatory review mechanism where key national partners and concerned UN agencies formally evaluate the project's design, budget availability and technical alignment. The expected outcome is a formal endorsement of the project document before submission to the Office of the Attorney General and National Treasury for approval. #16thJulyByelection #KuraYakoSautiYako #IEBCStrategicPlan #IEBCEOP

title: IEBC Commissioner Dr. Alutalala Joins African Dialogue on Election Observer Accreditation12th May 2026
text: Today, IEBC Commissioner Dr. Alutalala Mukhwana, Chairperson of the Voter Education, Partnerships, Communication and Stakeholder Engagement Committee, attended a Joint Dialogue on Citizen Election Observer Accreditation in Africa. The event brought together senior electoral commissioners and directors from Election Management Bodies (EMBs) in Ghana, Malawi, the Democratic Republic of Congo, South Africa, Nigeria, and Kenya to discuss strengthening accreditation frameworks for citizen election observers across the continent. While opening the roundtable discussion, Dr. Mukhwana noted that elections in Africa attract enormous public interest and expectation. He emphasized that election observation is no longer a ceremonial addition to the democratic process, but an integral part of electoral integrity. He added that the presence of observers helps simplify and communicate complex electoral processes to the public, thereby enhancing transparency, accountability, and trust in electoral administration. He further observed that EMBs and observer groups continue to face challenges such as administrative friction, scalability, and technological changes. He stated that IEBC is currently undertaking efforts to modernize its accreditation management systems, adding that such dialogues provide an important platform for progressive solutions and institutional reform. Dr. Alutalala underscored that despite differing national experiences, the shared objective remains the establishment of a gold standard for accreditation that balances the integrity and security of electoral processes with inclusivity and openness. He concluded by stressing that true democratic fidelity requires grassroots civil society organizations, community networks, and observer groups to have a place at the national democratic table. Mr. Richard Klein, Global Director for Elections at the National Democratic Institute (NDI), noted that EMBs and non-partisan citizen election observers have both built significant capacity over the past four decades in promoting credible elections. He added that while accreditation is intended to support transparent, participatory, and accountable elections, global trends show that the process is becoming increasingly complex, creating challenges for both EMBs and observer groups. The event serves as a platform for constructive networking and engagement between EMBs and citizen observer groups, reaffirming non-partisan citizen observation as a cornerstone of transparent and accountable elections across Africa.

title: IEBC Holds Election Operation Plan Validation Workshop Ahead of 2027 General Election9th May 2026
text: The Commission held an Election Operation Plan (EOP) 2025–2027 validation workshop. The EOP is a comprehensive document covering key electoral operations such as voter registration, boundary delimitation, technology deployment, logistics, staff recruitment and training, election security, as well as risk management and accountability frameworks to safeguard the integrity of the electoral cycle. Joyce Ekuam, Acting Director of Voter Education, Partnerships and Communications (DVEP&C), noted that voter registration is still ongoing at IEBC constituency offices, Huduma Centres, and the Customer Experience Centre at Anniversary Towers. She urged eligible citizens to turn out in large numbers and register as voters, emphasizing that voter registration is the gateway to democratic participation. Dr. Meshack Lomoywara, Acting Director of Research, Electoral Boundaries and Risk Management (DREB&RM), noted that the draft Election Operation Plan (EOP) is being reviewed during the workshop to ensure consensus before its official launch. He stated that the document will also undergo internal and external stakeholder validation before proceeding to the next phase for approval and adoption. He emphasized the importance of the team present at the workshop, noting that their contribution to the development of the plan is significant and should not be taken for granted. He also appreciated the participants for their commitment and input in shaping the document. Ruth Kulundu, DCS - Operations, while officially opening the workshop, noted that the 2027 General Election (#2027GE) will be a high-stakes election requiring high levels of public confidence in IEBC. She stated that the Commission’s role is to ensure elections are free from operational disruptions, with credible systems inorder to deliver peaceful and secure processes trusted by all stakeholders. She further emphasized that operational readiness must cover all counties, including remote areas, through adequate distribution of materials and proper training of personnel. She added that the Election Operation Plan (EOP) provides timelines for key activities and identifies responsible officers, strongly urging participants to remain focused and committed to strengthening preparedness for a credible electoral process.

title: IEBC Chairperson Rallies Elgeyo Marakwet Stakeholders to Boost Voter Registration Erastus Ethekon Leads Voter Registration Mobilization Drive in Elgeyo Marakwet25th Apr 2026
text: The Commission Chairperson Erastus Ethekon paid a courtesy call on the Elgeyo Marakwet County Governor, Wisley Kipyegon Rotich, and David Kosgei, County Commission, during his tour of Elgeyo Marakwet, as part of stakeholder engagement with local leaders and to provide support, quality assurance and oversight of the Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration (ECVR). During the engagement, Ethekon said elections start with a credible voters roll. As citizen, it’s your civic duty to participate in the election process to deepen our democracy. Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) will clean the register so as to have an inclusive and verified Register of Voters. He urged local leaders, the clergy and all stakeholders to support @IEBCKenya activities and link voter registration to services provided by government for the youth to feel essence of belonging. “Our Commissioners and staff are traversing the entire country to engage the people to understand their challenges and successes. Democracy is about a government by the people for the people. Register as a voter, exercise your voting right and elect a government of your choice,” said Ethekon. Governor Rotich observed that his government will go to the villages, especially on Saturday to Tuesday, to mobilise all remaining eligible citizens to come up and register as voters prior to the closure of the #ECVR2026 on 28th April, 2026. “There are many reasons why you need to enlist as a voter. Resource allocation from national and county government is pegged on the population. The bursary, roads, electricity and many other resources are shared based on numbers. So when we register, we will have our voice heard on the national resource sharing table.” Governor Rotich said that the County was strategizing on how to have 100 percent turnout for youth and all eligible people who wish to register, transfer their polling stations or change particulars can utilize the remaining days to visit registration centres. title: IEBC Vice Chairperson Fahima Araphat Rallies Taita Taveta Residents for Final Voter Registration Push25th Apr 2026
text: IEBC Vice Chairperson Fahima Araphat Abdallah, OGW was in Taita Taveta County holding a forum with State Actors to receive feedback and share ways to mobilize citizens to come out and register as voters. The meeting was preceded by a 2.5km walk in Voi town, where residents were mobilized to take part in the ongoing voter registration exercise. The Vice Chairperson called on all eligible Kenyans to take advantage of the remaining five days to register as voters and to surpass the set targets, stressing that elections are a continuous process that begins with registration. She urged citizens to participate actively while remaining peaceful and to reject any form of incitement that could undermine national unity. Speaking during the forum, the Vice Chairperson emphasized that peace and security remain the foundation of any successful electoral process, noting that instability in some regions locally and globally has shown how quickly lives, education and economic progress can be disrupted, hence the need to safeguard peace in the country. Drawing from experiences in Lamu and cases of students forced to return home from conflict affected countries, she noted that instability comes at a heavy personal and national cost, reinforcing the importance of maintaining peace especially during the electoral period. She also reaffirmed the Commission’s commitment to inclusivity and transparency, noting that no eligible voter will be left behind, including youth, women, persons with disabilities and inmates. She assured stakeholders that the Commission is prepared to deliver free, fair, inclusive, credible, and transparent elections, emphasizing that success will depend on the collective responsibility of all Kenyans to uphold peace and support the electoral process. Ag. CEM Taita Taveta County Christine Munga noted that the county’s vastness and remoteness continue to pose challenges to voter registration, while Deputy County Commissioner (DCC) Voi Mugo Gichiri assured that the administration will support the Commission and work closely with other stakeholders to ensure the success of the exercise. The meeting was attended by the DCC, Taita Taveta National Polytechnic (TTNP) Principal Shaw Fondo Kalama, the County Head of Security, County Heads of Departments including Education and the Registrar of Persons, administrative units comprising Chiefs and Assistant Chiefs, as well as IEBC staff from the county. #ECVR2026 #YourVoteYourFuture #14thMayByelections #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

title: IEBC Commissioner Dr. Ann Nderitu, CBS Calls for Public Trust and Institutional Strengthening at ICS Conference25th Apr 2026
text: IEBC Commissioner Dr. Ann Nderitu, CBS attended the Institute of Certified Secretaries (ICS) 30th Annual International Conference in Mombasa, themed “Resilient Governance for Thriving Economies.” Commissioner Dr. Ann took part in a panel discussion on rebuilding public trust in electoral institutions, alongside JLAC’s Chairperson Hon. George Gitonga Murugara, CBS (MP for Tharaka Constituency), Senior Counsel Charles Kanjama, President of the Law Society of Kenya (LSK), and Amb. FCS Dr. Koki Muli Grignon. Dr. Ann likened the electoral process to the role of a midwife, explaining that just as a midwife ensures the safe delivery of a child without determining the gender, the Commission facilitates the electoral process without influencing the outcome. This, she noted, underscores the Commission's commitment to delivering a transparent, credible, free, fair and inclusive electoral process. She highlighted the importance of shared responsibility in protecting electoral institutions. While public scrutiny is necessary, sustained attacks on institutions can weaken public confidence and hinder their effectiveness. She urged Kenyans to foster patience and trust in institutional processes while continuing to demand accountability. Dr. Ann also stressed the need to strengthen institutional capacity through continuous staff training, adequate resourcing and proper management of the Register of Voters (RoV) and election materials. She added that sufficient funding is critical, as elections are resource-intensive and require proper financial support to ensure effective implementation. She concluded by underscoring that credible elections depend on collaboration among all electoral stakeholders, including the government, the electoral body, voters, citizens, inter alia. She noted that such collaboration would ensure that IEBC delivers transparent, inclusive, free, fair elections, which are key to building public trust and strengthening democracy. #ECVR2026 #YourVoteYourFuture #14thMayByelections #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

title: IEBC Chairperson Leads CSR and Stakeholder Engagement in Turkana During ECVR25th Apr 2026
text: The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) Chairperson Erastus Ethekon together with Kenya Literature Bureau (KLB) Managing Director George Wanga, jointly undertook a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) by distributing textbooks, stationery and footballs to several schools that converged at RCEA Secondary School in Lokori, Turkana East Constituency during quality assurance and oversight of the Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration (ECVR). The Commission also held a stakeholder engagement forum and met with local youth groups, women groups, elders, marginalized communities, PWDs, CBO, religious leaders and Turkana Professional Association. The locals voiced their challenges in accessing voter registration centers owing to poor road network and insecurity. “We are here to listen to all Kenyans and your petitions will be reviewed and acted upon. IEBC’s verification portal is accurate and working and any voter can verify their details in the system using their mobile phones or online,” said Ethekon. The Chairperson said that the Commission had agreed not to stay in office, but to visit each part of the country to oversee the registration of voters and engage stakeholders including the national government to enhance issuance of national Identity Cards to make all Kenyans participate in the electoral process and have a legitimate and transparent 2027 General Election. Locals leaders shared challenges affecting Turkana County such as accessibility of registration centers, insecurity, boundaries and inclusion. However, the Chaiperson observed that without the required population number, there cannot be as many wards as communities want “Distribution of national resources requires numbers, even at county level the distribution is based on population,” he said. Ethekon urged Kenyans to come out register and be counted. He also called upon religious leaders to take the registration exercise seriously and ask their congregants to embrace the exercise. The Chairperson also took the opportunity to meet IEBCTurkana County staff led by County Elections Manager Amos Obonyo, who voiced their challenges and concerns in implementating #ECVR2026. Turkana county is among the top ten counties leading in new voter registration in the ongoing ECVR. Ethekon lauded the efforts put in place by the IEBC staff, the local leadership and all stakeholders in Turkana County to ensure ECVR is a success. The Commission targets to register over 2.5 million new voters during the ECVR, which ends on 28th April 2026. Thereafter, the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) will resume at the 57 Huduma centres, @IEBCKenya 290 constituencies across the country and Customer Experience Center at Anniversary Towers. Turkana East MP Nicholas Nixon Ngikolong, who handed a memorandum/petition to the chairperson, highlighted the challenges the constituents are enduring in a bid to access registration as voters under the ongoing ECVR exercise. The vast constituency covers roughly 70,000 square kilometres. #ECVR2026 #YourVoteYourFuture #14thMayByelections #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

title: IEBC Targets 2.5 Million New Voters in Enhanced Registration Drive30th Mar 2026
text: The Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration exercise will take place in the 30,619 gazetted registration centers countrywide that include the 57 Huduma centers. A kit movement schedule will be prepared in consultation with relevant stakeholders to determine how the kit will move around the County Assembly ward for the ECVR period. The Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration (ECVR) exercise targets to register approximately 2.5 million new voters. The exercise will bring registration services closer to citizens by moving from constituency offices to ward level and institutions of higher learning. The exercise targets to increase coverage by expanding enrollment, particularly for first-time registrants and youth, especially in under-registered or remote areas and also enhance inclusivity and equity to facilitate broader participation among marginalized groups. The Commission will make arrangements to have kits for universities and institutions of higher learning, in electoral areas where they are located to cater for students studying away from their home areas. Students are therefore not required to travel back home to be listed as voters. The registration kits stationed at the 57 Huduma Centers countrywide will be open such that anyone who wishes to register for the first time will be allowed to select a registration center of their choice and their details captured to the selected center. This will save Kenyans the trouble of having to travel long distances so as to be registered as a voter. The Commission will seek inter-agency collaboration by partnering with agencies like the National Registration Bureau (NRB) to fast-track the issuance of IDs, which are a legal prerequisite for voter registration. The requirement for one to be registered as a voter is that they should be a Kenyan citizen of majority age and with a national identification card or valid passport. The individual must present themselves physically to a registration officer as the registration process involves capturing biometric features and personal identifiable details of the applicant. #ECVR2026 #YourVoteYourFutureYourVoice #TalkWithIEBC #StopFakeNews

title: IEBC, Media Stakeholders Sign MoU to Strengthen Election Reporting Ahead of 202727th Mar 2026
text: The Commission today held a breakfast meeting on Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration (EVCR) and signing of the memorandum of understanding (MoU) between Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) and the Kenya Media Sector Working Group (KMSWG), which is a coalition of key media stakeholders. Speaking during the launch, Commission Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, who was accompanied by Members of the Commission, said the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) solidifies partnership in election reporting. “We have significant tasks ahead of us, particularly the management of the 2027 General Election. We are currently preparing for the Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration (ECVR), which will be launched on March 30, 2026, in Shimoni, Kwale County. Timely access to electoral information will be a priority, and IEBC will provide accurate and timely updates on all election-related matters during the electoral calendar we are currently implementing. We will also grant access to all polling centres and tallying centres for accredited journalists, who will receive training to understand their duties. We will create a platform for collaboration to explain to Kenyans how results are transmitted from polling stations to constituency tallying centers and ultimately to the national tallying center, to alleviate any anxiety in society. We agree on the importance of factchecking and holding the media accountable to verify information before publishing and broadcasting. “To the media, I urge you to go out and capture the stories of the ECVR and all other electoral processes, from the remotest villages in our country to the cities. Remember, this is our country, and we all have a role to play in making democracy work. Together, let us be objective and factual in our engagement and reporting. Let us encourage every Kenyan aged 18 and above, especially the youth, to register to vote. Let us promote peace throughout the electoral cycle violence has no place in democracy,” said Ethekon. We must all be accountable for our actions, as both the media and the IEBC. Those who call for accountability from the IEBC should also reflect on their own actions. Accountability is a two-way street, and everyone must play their part. Eric Oduor, the Kenya Union of Journalist Secretary General cautioned on the anticipated increase in disinformation and misinformation in the lead up to the 2027 General Election. He said the Commission needs to interact with the media in ways that go beyond just news gathering and reporting. “We hope that through our partnership, IEBC will set up a media centre with a fact-checking desk where journalists can work to counter fake news,” said Oduor. title: IEBC, KMSWG Hold Workshop to Review MOU Between IEBC and the Media10th Mar 2026
text: Today Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) Dr. Alutalala Mukhwana, Chairperson – Voter Education, Partnerships, Communication & Stakeholder Engagement Committee, brought together the Kenya Media Sector Working Group for a Workshop on Review of the MOU Between IEBC and the Media. Dr. Alutalala opened the workshop by highlighting the importance of a trust-based relationship between the media and IEBC. He noted that the media is critical in helping citizens understand how elections work, and countering dis/misinformation that can overshadow facts. Dr. Alutalala emphasized that restoring public confidence is as crucial as personal integrity and that elections begin long before polling day, “Help the public understand the work we do. Help them see the role of an electoral administrator. The media is essential in rebuilding public confidence in our democratic process,” he said. This MOU is more than a document. It’s a framework for partnership, a tool to empower journalists, and a pathway to a transparent, credible and inclusive election in 2027. Moses Sunkuli, OGW, Ag. Commission Secretary/CEO reflected on lessons from past elections, emphasizing that elections are a continuous process. Journalists must understand every stage—from voter registration and verification to results transmission—to ensure accurate reporting. “As we prepare for the 2027 General Election, this engagement is both timely and necessary. Elections take place within a dynamic information environment where facts, narratives and public trust interact and shape public perception. In that space, the partnership between the electoral management body and the media is indispensable,” he said. Felix Oduor, Executive Director, ELGIA, highlighted the historical role of media in Kenya’s electoral process, noting that collaborative engagement between electoral bodies and the media has precedent both locally and internationally. He emphasized that such partnerships enhance transparency and public trust, citing examples from previous elections and comparative experiences from Ghana and the United States. Felix stressed that while challenges exist, particularly around timing and coordination, a well-structured framework for media engagement can significantly strengthen electoral integrity and ensure that the public receives accurate, timely information. Zubeidah Kananu, President of KEG, emphasized the diversity of the media sector and the responsibility it carries. "Through this MOU, we ensure journalists are trained, informed, and ready to report elections responsibly, minimizing misinformation and conflict,", she noted. Martin Maasai, Trustee at KEG and Chairperson of the Media Freedoms & Ethics Committee, reflected on the current state of the media industry, noting the rapid turnover of experienced journalists and the prevalence of younger reporters covering elections for the first time. He stressed the importance of creating spaces for engagement and training between the media and the IEBC, ensuring journalists understand the full electoral process—from voter registration to the announcement of results. Maasai emphasized that responsible and informed reporting is essential for transparency, public confidence and preventing misinformation, reminding participants that “journalists do what they do precisely because they care about this country.” Victor Bwire, Director of Media Training and Development, MCK, highlighted the collaborative efforts already underway between MCK and IEBC to train journalists on electoral processes and responsible election reporting. He noted the challenges posed by Kenya’s vast media landscape, with hundreds of radio, TV, digital and blog platforms, emphasizing that standardized training and clear guidelines are essential for consistent, accurate coverage. Bwire also spoke on emerging issues like artificial intelligence, digital media, and user-generated content, explaining that the new Code of Ethics and the “Introduction to Media Practice” course aim to equip all media practitioners—including non-journalists—with the skills to report ethically and professionally. He concluded by stressing that coordinated reporting, journalist safety, and adherence to standards are critical for enhancing public trust and credibility in elections. The workshop reinforced the partnership between IEBC and the media, ensuring journalists are equipped to safeguard credible, transparent and peaceful elections in 2027.

title: IEBC, ELGIA Spearhead Multi Sector Electoral Law Reforms to Strengthen 2027 Polls18th Feb 2026
text: Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) led by Commissioner MaryKaren Sorobit, Chairperson, Legal Compliance and Political Parties Liaison Committee, in collaboration with ELGIA, is engaging stakeholders in a comprehensive electoral legal reform initiative aimed at fortifying governance and ensuring integrity in the electoral process ahead of the 2027 General Election. Describing the initiative as a key milestone in the post-2022 reform journey, Sorobit noted that the process builds on gaps identified after the 2017 General Election and reflects the Commission’s sustained commitment to strengthening the legal, administrative and regulatory framework underpinning Kenya’s elections. The reform package covers proposed amendments to the Elections Act, Election Offences Act, County Governments Act, campaign financing laws, a proposed Referendum Bill and regulations governing voter registration, voter education, party primaries and lists, election technology and campaign financing. “This is not a narrow legislative adjustment, but a structural effort to reinforce electoral governance, close legal gaps, and enhance enforceability well ahead of 2027,” she emphasized. A Multi-Sectoral Working Group, including representatives from the Kenya Law Reforms Commission, ORPP, AG, PPLC, JCE, PPDT, The National Assembly, Katiba Institute, ELOG, Transparency International, ICJ, has been established to guide the consultations and public participation process aimed at refining the draft Bills. By promoting collaboration among key election stakeholders, the Commission aims to ensure that the proposals are well-informed and aligned with the legal framework. The team is expected to fast-track the refinement and submission of the legislative instruments to Parliament in good time before the 2027 General Election. BonMak Olwal, Program Manager, UKAID, representing ELGIA, reaffirmed support for strengthening democratic governance through collaborative reform and urged stakeholders to actively contribute to enriching the proposed laws. #26thFebByelections | #YourVoteYourFuture | #TalkwithIEBC | #StopFakeNews

title: IEBC and LSK Strengthen Partnership to Safeguard Electoral Integrity16th Feb 2026
text: Today, the Law Society of Kenya (LSK), led by its President Faith Odhiambo, paid a courtesy call to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) . The Commission led by Chairperson Erastus Ethekon welcomed the LSK delegation and underscored the importance of the engagement. IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, HSC noted that the LSK is a key institution within Kenya’s governance framework. He emphasized thatIEBC occupies a critical position in the country’s governance architecture, with a clear constitutional mandate to manage elections, referenda and boundary delimitation processes. He acknowledged the vital role LSK has played in advancing reforms in Kenya and stated that the Commission cannot effectively discharge its mandate without close collaboration with the Society. He observed that the meeting was particularly important for the new Commission as it seeks to strengthen partnerships and explore practical ways of supporting each another in delivering the respective mandates. The Chairperson further affirmed that the Commission welcomes constructive criticism. He stated that feedback that helps to improve processes, systems and the manner in which the Commission executes its public mandate is always encouraged. Addressing the LSK delegation, he reiterated the Commission’s openness to listen, learn and work together in moving the country forward. Following the by-elections, the Commission conducted a comprehensive post-election review involving stakeholders such as security agencies, political parties, candidates and civil society organizations inter alias. The review examined what worked well, identified areas that required improvement and generated lessons to inform future electoral processes. IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, HSC observed that the Commission also took note of concerns raised by stakeholders regarding the presence of gangs around polling areas, incidents of voter intimidation and harassment, electoral violence, and voter bribery. He noted that such acts are unlawful and undermine the integrity of the electoral process. While the Code of Conduct Enforcement Committee is mandated to address violations of the Electoral Code of Conduct, it can only take action upon receipt of a formal complaint. “The Commission therefore urges candidates, political parties, and members of the public to promptly report any breaches to enable appropriate action to be taken in accordance with the law, as it remains committed to ensuring peaceful, transparent, and credible elections,” he said. The Chairperson cautioned against rhetoric that undermines public confidence in the electoral body, stating: “If political leaders portray the Commission as compromised, their supporters may lose faith in the process and choose not to register or vote, believing that their participation is meaningless. We must therefore work together to support the Commission in delivering free, fair, inclusive, transparent and credible elections.” Faith Odhiambo, President of the Law Society of Kenya, expressed appreciation to the IEBC Chairperson and Commissioners for convening the meeting, noting the longstanding partnership between LSK and the Commission anchored on the rule of law and constitutionalism. She recalled that in the 2022GE, the Commission maintained an open door policy that allowed LSK to provide input on electoral laws and reforms, even under tight timelines and significant operational pressure. She reaffirmed LSK’s commitment to supporting necessary legal reforms, including campaign financing laws, to enhance the integrity and smooth conduct of elections. Odhiambo emphasized that sustained stakeholder support is essential to strengthening Kenya’s electoral processes. On judicial engagement, she called for closer collaboration between the Commission and the Judiciary to minimize last minute court orders that often disrupt electoral timelines and create uncertainty for candidates and voters. Odhiambo further proposed joint Continuing Professional Development (CPD) sessions to enhance electoral knowledge among advocates, particularly young lawyers. She underscored the importance of broader public awareness through radio, observing that while Gen Z is active on social media, a significant portion of Kenyans still rely on traditional media platforms for information. In this regard, she noted that LSK plans to conduct nationwide civic education in September and October through LSK Legal Awareness Week, including the distribution of pamphlets covering key topics to be agreed upon with the Commission. "On the issue of disinformation, we must invest significantly in media monitoring and rapid response, especially to tackle AI-generated and manipulated content that disproportionately targets female candidates. Structured engagement with digital platforms is crucial to ensure swift action against users spreading harmful content," said Odhiambo. She concluded by emphasizing the continued partnership between LSK and the Commission in areas including election observation, accreditation, and electoral reform. #26thFebByelections | #YourVoteYourFuture | #TalkwithIEBC | #StopFakeNews

title: IEBC Joins KBC in Celebrating World Radio Day, Urges Youth to Register and Participate in Elections11th Feb 2026
text: The Commission today joined KBC to celebrate World Radio Day at their HQ in Nairobi. World Radio Day is a globally recognized event aimed at celebrating radio broadcast, improve international cooperation among radio broadcasters and encourage decision-making. The Commission was represented by Commissioner Dr. Alutalala Mukhwana, Chair of the Voter Education, Partnerships, Communications, and Stakeholder Engagement Committee (VEPSEC), who delivered a keynote speech on the importance of radio in election management. In his address, Commissioner Mukhwana emphasized that radio remains the most accessible and trusted medium for reaching citizens across the country, particularly young people, marginalized communities, and those in remote areas. He noted that radio continues to play a central role in voter education, civic awareness, and the dissemination of accurate electoral information. The Commissioner used the platform to urge young Kenyans to actively participate in the electoral process by registering as voters and turning out to vote when elections are held. He observed that youth participation in voter registration remains low, despite young people constituting a significant proportion of the country’s population. “While technology continues to evolve, citizens must use the systems available today to shape their future. We should not delay participation while waiting for future innovations,” Commissioner Dr Alutalala said. He addressed concerns raised by some young people who perceive the current voting system as outdated, clarifying that electoral participation should not be hindered by the absence of mobile or phone-based voting. Drawing parallels with the evolution of radio and music technology, he noted that meaningful progress is achieved by making the best use of existing tools. Commissioner Dr Alutalala informed participants that IEBC will roll out an enhanced voter registration exercise in March across the country. The exercise will ensure services reach communities at the grassroots level. He further dismissed claims that elections can be easily manipulated, stating that the Commission has put in place robust voter identification and verification measures, including the use of national identity cards, biometric fingerprint verification, and iris recognition. “The voting procedures currently in place makes it impossible for an unregistered person to vote. The system is secure and designed to protect the integrity of the electoral process,” he said. Commissioner Dr Alutalala assured Kenyans that the 2027 General Election will be peaceful, free, fair and credible, and encouraged all eligible citizens to register and vote in order to actively participate in determining the country’s future. The Commissioner was taken through the history of radio from 1927 to the present day, highlighting key milestones and technological advancements that have transformed radio broadcasting over the years. The presentation underscored how innovations in technology have expanded radio’s reach, improved content delivery, and enhanced its continued relevance in an evolving media landscape.

title: IEBC Trains Trainers of Trainers(ToTs) Ahead of 26th February By-Elections6th Feb 2026
text: Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) is currently training Trainers of Trainers (ToTs) in preparation for the upcoming by-elections scheduled for 26th February 2026. Opening the workshop on behalf of the Chairperson, Commissioner Hassan Noor Hassan, observed that just as sermons are repeated because human memory is fallible, we are reaffirming our mandate, values, and responsibilities. "While elections are a collective responsibility, the credibility of the process rests squarely on our shoulders. We cannot afford to let Kenyan downs who expect us to deliver peaceful, fair, free and credible by-elections," he said. Commissioner Hassan noted that the Commission had over the past six months engaged widely with stakeholders across the political, security, judicial, and civil spectrum; and the message had been consistent: "deliver a fair election". "It is my firm belief that the upcoming by-elections will be the most peaceful, credible, and transparent this country has witnessed. I am confident that we have officers in the field capable of delivering this mandate. Consistency and strict adherence to the law and procedures are non-negotiable," observed Commissioner Hassan. The Ag. Commission Secretary/CEO, Moses Sunkuli, OGW, expressed his appreciation to the Commission and called for support. "As I have already conveyed my commitment to the Commission, I equally appeal for your support as we embark on the journey of revamping and resetting the Commission as we head to the 2027 General Election. Change is inevitable. We must find new and better ways of doing things to deliver effectively to the people of Kenya," said Sunkuli. He also highlighted that preparing poll officials is key to ensuring high-quality election services. The training will cover all aspects of election operations, from pre-polling to polling and post-polling, including proper procedures, the use of electronic voter identification, managing results, and full compliance with legal and regulatory requirements. #26thFebByElections #TalkwithIEBC #StopFakeNews #YourVote YourFuture

title: IEBC and Nation Media Group Discuss Collaboration on Responsible Electoral Reporting5th Feb 2026
text: Today, Nation Media Group led by its Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Mr. Geoffrey Odundo, paid a courtesy call to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) to discuss areas of collaboration ahead of the 2027 General Election. Speaking during the engagement, IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon , emphasized the importance of responsible electoral communication, noting that while transparency and public-interest reporting are essential, messaging must be handled carefully to maintain public trust and participation. “As a public institution, we do not shy away from reporting legitimate issues. However, the framing and amplification of certain matters can sometimes unintentionally discourage voter participation or weaken confidence in the electoral process,” said Ethekon. The Chairperson highlighted challenges in mobilising resources for voter education and peace campaigns, observing that perceptions of adequate funding often limit support for critical communication initiatives. “To deliver a peaceful and credible election, we must invest deliberately in voter education and peace building. This cannot be achieved by the Commission alone and must be a collective national effort,” he said. The Chairperson observed there was need for a cooperative framework involving the media, civil society, and the private sector to jointly support phased peace and civic education initiatives, with the Commission committing to play its part. Mr. Odundo reiterated Nation Media Group’s civic responsibility to inform the public accurately and responsibly, describing the media as an “underwriter of democracy.” He expressed interest in collaborating with the Commission on civic education, timely dissemination of information, and effective results transmission to enhance public confidence during elections. The meeting ended by underscoring the importance of sustained collaboration in safeguarding Kenya’s stability as we prepare for the 2027 General Election. #26thFebByElections #TalkwithIEBC #StopFakeNews #YourVoteYourFuture

title: IEBC to support women bridge gender gap in elective positions during 2027GE23rd Dec 2025
text: The Commission, represented by Vice Chairperson Fahima Araphat Abdallah, OGW, last week, joined the Association of Media Women in Kenya (AMWIK) and the Friedrich Naumann Foundation Kenya(FNF-Kenya) to launch a research report titled: “Bridging the Gender Gap Towards Kenya’s 2027 Elections.” The report in its findings, noted that despite the transformative aspirations of the 2010 Constitution, women currently hold only 23.9% of parliamentary seats well below the constitutional threshold. title: IEBC condemns violence and disruption of voting process witnessed during byelections in Kasipul, Mbeere and Malava6th Dec 2025
text: The Commission noted with grave concern the incidents of violence, intimidation, and disruption reported in parts of the country during the 27th November, 2025 by-elections and condemned in the strongest terms possible the acts of violence, hooliganism and lawlessness experienced in some electoral areas. Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC noted that the acts of violence violated Article 81(e) of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010, which requires that elections be free from violence, intimidation, improper influence, or corruption and undermined the principles of Article 86 on the conduct of simple, accurate, verifiable, secure, accountable, and transparent elections. “Elections are a democratic exercise, and no individual or group has the right to compromise the peace, safety, or integrity of the process. We are working closely with security agencies to ensure swift action against any perpetrators. It is important that all political actors must uphold the principles of peaceful participation and respect for the rule of law,” said Ethekon. During the just concluded by-election, the percentage of voter turnout by each the 5 constituencies and Baring’o county was commendable. Baring’o Senate election had 25.97% voter turnout, Member of National Assembly (MNA) for Magarini (34.7%), Mbeere North (61.9%), Malava (46.26%), Ugunja (25%), Kasipul (46.4%) and Banissa (35.7%). The Chairperson urged the voters to come out in large numbers to vote noting that their vote was their voice and that participation in the polling process strengthens Kenya’s democracy and every ballot contributes to a transparent and credible outcome. The Commission also pronounced itself on misinformation that circulated claims alleging ballot stuffing in some polling stations. “These claims are false, unfounded, and intended to mislead the public. All polling stations operated under strict procedures that included the presence of agents from participating political parties, accredited observers and security personnel. Every ballot issued corresponded to a verified voter, and all processes remained open to scrutiny. “The public should always rely on official communication from the Commission and refrain from sharing unverified information that would undermine public confidence in the electoral process. The Commission remains committed to delivering a transparent, peaceful, and credible by-election. I thank all voters, officials, agents, and observers for their continued cooperation. Violence and intimidation have no place in our democracy. We call on security agencies to act firmly where breaches occur.

title: IEBC develops Strategic Communication Plan to align with new trends and enhance delivery of electoral information4th Dec 2025
text: The Commission, supported by the Electoral Law and Governance Institute for Africa (ELGIA), reviewed the enhanced Strategic Communication Plan to guide the effective dissemination of electoral information, strengthen stakeholder confidence and keep pace with emerging communication trends, technologies, and lessons learned over the years. Commission Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC accompanied by fellow Commissioners during the workshop, emphasized that this strategic review reflects the Commission’s deliberate and focused steps to enhance its communication. “Developing the enhanced Strategic Communication Plan at this time is critical. With new technologies, the growing influence of digital platforms, and rising challenges such as misinformation, this revision allows the Commission to strengthen its communication with both internal and external stakeholders,” said Chairperson Ethekon. A robust communication framework will enable the Commission to address challenges before they escalate and maintain credibility, inclusivity, and a shared sense of purpose within the organization. It also aims to improve internal communication so that all staff members move forward with common understanding and unity of purpose. Dr. Alutalala Mukhwana who is the Chairperson of the Voter Education, Partnerships, Communications, and Stakeholder Engagement Committee, highlighted that the main challenge in communication is being able to harness collective experiences to determine the right moments for Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) on when? how and what to communicate. “For too long, we have relied on a enhanced Strategic Communication Plan from 2013 which is now outdated in today’s fast-evolving digital age. Persisting with this old framework would be like driving the nation’s democratic vehicle into a thick fog at Mai Mahiu with dimmed headlights,” remarked Dr. Alutalala. The Chairperson noted that from the Post-ElectionEvaluation (PEE) Report, especially the Observers’ reports, it was Communication that was picked out as an area that required improvement and in today’s fast-paced information environment, how the Commission communicate shapes how people perceive IEBC and the confidence they have in the institution. It’s not just about issuing press statements or appearing in the media — it’s about staying engaged, being transparent, and managing our reputation with consistency and honesty. That’s why strong and proactive communication is so critical in realizing our vision as a Commission. “Developing the enhanced Strategic Communication Plan couldn’t have come at a better time. With new technologies, the growing influence of digital platforms and challenges like misinformation, this review gives the Commission a chance to strengthen how it communicates to internally and externally stakeholders. A solid communication framework will not only help the Commission handle challenges before they escalate but also ensure it maintain credibility, inclusivity and a shared sense of purpose within the organization. It’s also about improving how we talk to each other internally — so that we all move in the same direction, with common understanding and unity of purpose. “By aligning our communication efforts with our core functions, we’ll improve the quality, timeliness, and impact of our messages — whether to the public, the media, or our partners. We’re not just updating a document — we’re shaping how IEBC tells its story, builds trust, and delivers on its mission to strengthen democracy in Kenya,” said Ethekon. Felix Odhiambo, the Executive Director of ELGIA, commended IEBC Commissioners on how speedy they hit the ground upon their inductions over three months ago by identifying five areas that needed immediate support being legal reforms, strategic communication, boundaries review, voter education and voter registration. “I’m happy to report that there has been remarkable progress in four out of the five areas (save for Boundaries Delimitation). Feedback received from Kenyans in our interactions and development partners is positive underlining the robust and good improvement and lets us keep up the momentum. This team will interact and enrich the draft, subject it to external validation to make it better and hopefully IEBC Plenary will adopt the enhanced Strategic Communication Plan.

title: IEBC ready to conduct by-elections, reaches out to candidates to hold peaceful campaigns and meetings4th Dec 2025
text: The Commission has come out to assure the country that plans for the 29th November, 2005 By-Elections in 22 Electoral areas. Speaking while addressing the media at Anniversary towers, Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon assured the country that the forthcoming By elections will be free fair and accountable. “The IEBC has finalized key activities, including the recruitment and training of polling officials, and the deployment of logistical support teams across all electoral areas. Dispatch of election materials is ongoing and will be completed in good time for the polls” said Ethekon. Pursuant to the provisions of Article 81 of the Constitution, the Commission is required to conduct free and fair elections devoid of violence, intimidation, improper influence, or corruption. The Commission also issued a stern warning to perpetrators of violence that, the Commission will invoke the law, that gives a number of actions that can be taken by the Commission against the perpetrators of electoral violence. In a bid to address the security challenges in some of the electoral areas, the commission held a joint meeting with National Police Service and National Cohesion and Integration Commission (NCIC)and issued a joint statement to reaffirm their joint commitment to delivering peaceful, transparent, and credible by-elections that reflect the will of the people and uphold the integrity of Kenya’s democratic institutions. Pursuant to these provisions, and informed by the prevailing security situation, the Commission in collaboration with the NPS and NCIC called upon the Political Parties and Candidates to conduct peaceful campaigns and strictly adhere to their campaign schedules and the Electoral Code of Conduct. The Commission went ahead to summon two candidates in the Kaipul by election to face the code of conduct enforcement committee on their possible involvement in security challenges being witnessed in the Constituency. Any breach SHALL attract sanctions as prescribed in the available legislative framework. The Commission Chairperson assured the nation that all critical activities for the by-elections are on course, including the recruitment and training of polling officials, the ongoing dispatch of election materials, all set to be completed ahead of polling day. Following rising political tensions and violence, particularly in Kasipul, the IEBC has intensified coordination with the National Police Service (NPS) and the National Cohesion and Integration Commission (NCIC), issuing a joint statement to assure Kenyans of robust security arrangements to guarantee the integrity of the upcoming elections. Violence. IEBC has condemned electoral violence and warned it will take stern action, including campaign suspensions and issuing summons to enforce the Electoral Code of Conduct. This week, two candidates from Kasipul constituency were summoned to appear before the Commission’s code of conduct enforcement committee to answer for their possible involvement in violent incidents. Any breach of the code will attract strict sanctions as prescribed by law. The Commission urges all political parties and candidates to run peaceful campaigns, adhere to officially scheduled campaign times, and strictly follow the Electoral Code of Conduct. The chairman encouraged Voters to turn out in large numbers and elect leaders of their choice in the By- election areas. The chairperson reiterated the Commission’s resolve to uphold Kenya’s constitutional mandate and guaranteed a free, fair, and peaceful elections.

title: IEBC joins inter agency forum on data sharing framework to support Continuous Voter Registration exercise11th Nov 2025
text: The Commission participated in an interagency meeting to explore Data Sharing framework strategies that will support the ongoing Voter Registration (CVR) exercise. The team seeks to develop a collaborative framework and draft a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the IEBC and the State Department of Immigration and Citizen Services for secure and lawful data sharing. This should cover access to data on national Identity Cards and Passports, Integrated Population Registration System (IPRS), Records of deceased persons and other relevant datasets for the purpose of updating the Register of Voters. The IEBC team was led by Director Electoral Operations Moses Sunkuli, Director Legal Services (DLS) Chrispine Owiye and Director Information Communication Technology (DICT) Michael Ouma. Speaking during the event, Sunkuli reiterated that the CVR exercise is a vital step in ensuring that every eligible Kenyan has the opportunity to participate in shaping the country’s future through democratic elections. The exercise is particularly directed towards young people who have recently attained 18 years, and all citizens who have not yet registered or need to update their voter information. NRB Secretary Dr Chrstopher Wanjau and team leader said the bureau targets to register over 6.7 million Kenyans by 2027. “We produce National Identity Cards every day and it would be ideal for the IEBC staff to seize the opportunity and have close proximity to the youth, who visit our Bureau offices to collect IDs, to register them straight away,” said Wanjau. The Bureau also confirmed that thousands of ID cards that have not been collected from their offices and sought collaboration and teamwork to whip up citizens to collect them. The meeting agreed to form join secretariat to actualize an API to IPRS Integrated Population Registration System that will come in handy in the pre-registration module.

title: IEBC undertakes capacity building for Commissioners to enhance understanding of polling process ahead of by-elections11th Nov 2025
text: The Commission undertook capacity building for Chairperson, Vice Chairperson and members of the Commission on electoral processes in a special workshop hosted in Mombasa.. The capacity building session, organized by the Directorate of Electoral Operations through the Electoral Training Departmen, was meant to enlighten the Commissioners to diligently deliver on IEBC Constitutional mandate, one of them being the forthcoming 24 by-elections set to be conducted on 27th November 2025 across the country. Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan Hussein Marjan emphasised the importance of Commissioners understanding the electoral process.. “We’re now delving into the mechanics of our work: how elections and referenda are conducted, how voter registration is managed, how technology enhances these processes and how all these elements combine to ensure credible elections.”. Commissioner Anne Nderitu, CBS who is the Chairperson of the Electoral Operations Committee, encouraged the trainees to carefully interrogate the presentations as it is the backbone of election management. She emphasized that the Commission has a rich knowledge base to deliver the tailored content.. During the closing ceremony, the Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC expressed satisfaction with the Commission’s internal trainers. He encouraged the CEO to institutionalize a knowledge management centre to facilitate ongoing knowledge transfer and experience sharing within the Commission.. Further, the Chairperson urged the Commission to expand training to external stakeholders in the electoral sector, ensuring they remain well-informed and actively engaged with the electoral sub-system.. The customised training was designed to equip the Commissioners with hands-on knowledge and experience in electoral-legal framework, voter registration, conduct of elections, results management, election technology, stakeholder engagement, communication among others. These initiatives underscore the Commission’s dedication to enhance public trust and strengthen Kenya’s democracy.

title: IEBC scoops the Best Independent Commission Stand Award at the 2025 Nairobi International Trade Fair20th Oct 2025

title: IEBC develops Medium-Term Expenditure Framework, pledges to observe prudent financial planning and accountability20th Oct 2025
text: The Commission led by Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC, convened at the serane Sawela Lodges in Naivasha from 22nd to 26th September 2025 to develop its Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) for the financial years 2026/27, 2027/28, and 2028/29. The Chaiperson observed that at the heart of the budget preparation process is a commitment to prudent financial planning, expenditure and accountability guaranteeing value for money while enhancing service delivery. While opening the workshop, Ethekon noted: “History reminds us that credible elections are not born on Election Day. They are built here in strategic meetings like this, where planning meets responsibility.” The Chairperson underscored the need for integrity in budgeting and to help the country manage election costs by optimizing scarce resources without compromising quality. “When we work on these numbers, they must not be arbitrary. Every proposal must be realistic, rational and aligned with our institutional goals. The budget we shape here is not just about figures it is the blueprint for building trust, credibility and confidence in our electoral process,” said Ethekon. The Commission’s Vice-Chairperson, Ms. Fahima Araphat Abdallah, OGW, who chairs the Finance & Procurement Committee, emphasized that the workshop marks the foundation of financial planning and electoral readiness for the next three years. She emphasized on the need to create a budget that complies with National Treasury circular, supports IEBC operations, reflects economic realities, and upholds the Commission’s constitutional mandate. The 10th August 2027 General Election falls within the current MTEF and the Commission has begun engaging the National Treasury as well as committees of parliament to ensure timely planning, allocation and disbursement of funds for the preparation and management of elections.

title: IEBC meets Political Parties Liaison Committee to enhance collaboration, provides update on conduct of by-elections19th Oct 2025
text: The Commission led by Chairman Erastus Ethekon and supported by Elgia Afric held an introductory meeting with the Political Parties Liaison Committee (PPLC). The PPLC serves as a platform for dialogue and collaboration between the Commission and the Office of the Registrar of Political Parties, in accordance with paragraph 9(2) of the Second Schedule of the IEBC Act, Cap 7C, and section 38 of the Political Parties Act, Cap 7D. The Commission’s engagement with the PPLC aimed to enhance collaboration by introducing the Commission to political parties, providing an update on preparations for the upcoming by-elections, sharing plans and timelines for the commencement of Continuous Voter Registration and discussing structured modalities for future interactions between the Commission and political parties.. “We come together not as separate entities but as partners united by a common responsibility to protect the will of the Kenyan people through credible, peaceful and inclusive elections,” said Ethekon. Ethekon observed that since the Commission came onboard, it had been on a significant learning journey by engaging stakeholders. “We began by meeting the Steering Committee of the PPLC, recognizing that every political party, regardless of size, plays a crucial role in fostering public trust in the electoral process. Hence, today’s plenary meeting is of great importance,” he noted. Commissioner MaryKaren Sorobit, Chairperson of the Legal Compliance and Political Liaison Committee, welcomed representatives from all political parties to the meeting. “Your presence emphasizes the importance of partnership in safeguarding the credibility and integrity of our elections,” she remarked. Commissioner Marykaren emphasized that the meeting aims to establish a framework for a sustained partnership. Evans Misati, the Chairperson of the PPLC, highlighted the invaluable role of the committee in promoting dialogue, building consensus and promoting political tolerance. This is particularly crucial as the country gears up for the upcoming by-elections and the launch of Continuous Voter Registration on Monday, alongside other significant functions of the Commission that will take place in the near future. Ms. Sophia Sitati, Ag. Registrar of Political Parties, called upon the three institutions to collaborate continuously to ensure that democracy is strengthened through coordinated efforts, transparent processes and inclusive participation. “As we look to the future, the voices of political parties are vital in shaping the quality and credibility of our elections. May you act as ambassadors of the Commission, promoting transparency, integrity and peaceful democratic participation within your parties and the broader public,” said Sitati. Marjan underscored that IEBC values the PPLC not merely as a statutory body or a formality but as an essential forum for strengthening Kenya’s democracy and good electoral governance.

title: Commission targets 6.3 million new voters on resumption of Continuous Voter Registration exercise29th Sep 2025
text: The Commission Chairperson, Erastus Edung Ethekon, has assured the public that IEBC is fully prepared and working diligently for the forthcoming by-elections as a precursor to the 2027 General Election. He emphasized that preparations for the by-elections are on course. On resumption of Continuous Voter Registration, the Chairperson stated that the Commission aims to enlist 6.3 million new eligible voters, 70 percent of whom are youth. This assurance came during his appearance before the Parliamentary Accounts Committee, led by Butere Member of the National Assembly Hon. Tindi Mwale, where the Commission had been invited to respond to the Auditor General’s report on Account of the National Government for the Financial year ended 30th June 2023. The Chairperson also pledged to maintain close collaboration with the leadership of both houses of Parliament and the various committees, as well as other stakeholders. “We have an open-door policy and remain committed to working closely with the leadership of both houses of Parliament and all progressive Kenyans to enhance our electoral processes and voter experience,” said Ethekon.

title: IEBC identifies, tutors Training of Trainers ahead of national launch of Continuous Voter Registration exercise19th Sep 2025
text: The Commission Secretary/CEO Hussein Marjan Hussein, MBS, on 9th September, 2025 opened the National Training of Trainers (ToTs) workshop for the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR). Training program, was tailor made in preparation for the resumption of the CVR exercise, which will launched in Kajiado County on 29th September, 2025. “As we formally begin the Training of Trainers for the upcoming Continuous Voter Registration exercise, this workshop marks a pivotal step in the Commission’s journey toward delivering a credible and inclusive 2027 General Election,” he said. According to Article 88(4)(b) of the Constitution of Kenya, the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission is mandated to conduct continuous voter registration and regularly revise the voter register. This is not a discretionary task; it is a constitutional and legal duty that we must execute with both urgency and excellence. This training was not merely a scheduled event but it represented a strategic investment in the credibility of Kenya’s democracy. He urged participants to uphold integrity. “Integrity is not a suggestion, it is a condition of service,” said Marjan. The CEO emphasized that every decision and action must reflect the highest standards of honesty, impartiality and professionalism, as public trust in this institution is earned and is a collective responsibility. The training workshop addressed all aspects of the CVR process, from operational procedures to the technical details of the new Kenya Integrated Election Management System’s (KIEMS) voter registration module. The approach targeted to ensure consistency and standardization of electoral operations across all levels and offices of the Commission. Additionally, it will facilitate a uniform application of electoral laws, procedures, and technologies while enhancing preparedness and risk management for the CVR exercise. This training program is designed for both field Registration Officers and headquarters staff. The Master Trainers, responsible for developing the training content, will act as the lead trainers for the (ToTs) program. Afterwards, the ToTs will train registration officers in the to prepare for the resumption of the CVR exercise. The objective is to ensure that all levels of the Commission are fully equipped and ready for the start of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) process.

title: IEBC pays courtesy call on Prime Cabinet Secretary, discusses progress and priorities in preparation for 2027 GE19th Sep 2025
text: IEBC, led by Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, HSC, paid a courtesy call on the Prime Cabinet Secretary and Cabinet Secretary for Foreign and Diaspora Affairs, H.E. Dr. Hon Musalia W Mudavadi, EGH, at his office. IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, HSC conveyed warm regards to the Office of the Prime Cabinet Secretary and Cabinet Secretary for Foreign and Diaspora Affairs, while highlighting the Commission’s progress and priorities as it prepares for the 2027 General Election. He noted that since assuming office, the Commission has undergone a comprehensive induction process that equipped its members with the skills required to deliver credible elections. To enhance efficiency, roles have been distributed among commissioners, each heading a committee aligned to the institution’s mandate. The Chairperson further underscored the Commission’s commitment to stakeholder engagement, citing recent consultations with the heads of missions at the British High Commission, the Media Council of Kenya, civil society organizations, security stakeholders in Mombasa, the Judicial Service Commission and the Head of Public Service. Others were the Cabinet Secretary to the Treasury, the Political Parties Liaison Committee, the National Cohesion and Integration Commission, the British High Commissioner, the UNDP Resident Representative, and other governance partners. These engagements, he explained, have been critical in fostering inclusivity and building synergies for free, fair, credible, and peaceful elections. He also emphasized the importance of collaboration with the Ministry of Foreign and Diaspora Affairs in engaging diaspora voters through voter registration and civic education. Additionally, he appealed for whole-ofgovernment support, particularly in the timely and adequate resourcing of the Commission. This, he noted, would ensure smooth operations, robust civic education, enhanced security measures, and strengthened inter-agency coordination. The Chairperson disclosed that the Commission has sought concurrence from the Prime Cabinet Secretary and the Cabinet Secretary for Foreign and Diaspora Affairs to allow the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) to extend support to the Commission. This will be preceded by a Needs Assessment Mission aimed at identifying priority areas where the UN and development partners can provide coordinated and timely electoral assistance, in line with the electoral cycle approach. “As a Commission, we are determined to deliver credible elections, but this requires adequate resourcing, strong partnerships, and timely support across government and with our development partners,” said Chairperson. Mudavadi congratulated the commissioners for their appointment and told them that serving Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) was a privilege. He asked the commissioners to serve with humility, resilience and forthrightness. “Do not compromise on your independence as an EMB. Ensure you live up to the expectations of the Kenyan people by conducting free, fair, and credible elections,” said Mudavadi. He assured the Commission of his office’s support and facilitation in meeting its requirements, particularly in matters relating to engagement with the diaspora community. In particular, the PCS assured IEBC of his support in accessing, enhancing and optimizing diaspora participation in electoral process; and in liasing with the relevant state and non state actors, including international community, in raising requisite resource support.

title: IEBC engages security agents, targets peaceful, credible and secure elections14th Sep 2025
text: The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), led by its Chairperson, Erastus Edung Ethekon, 5th September, 2025 held a strategic engagement with security agencies from Mombasa, Kilifi, and Kwale Counties. The meeting sought to strengthen collaboration as the Commission embarks on key electoral activities, including the resumption of Continuous Voter Registration (CVR), the conduct of by-elections, and other planned operations within the electoral calendar. In his opening remarks, the Chairperson emphasized that the Commission’s responsibility goes beyond the administration of elections. “As a Commission, our duty goes beyond administering elections; it extends to safeguarding fairness, credibility, and peace in the electoral process,” he stated. He further noted that since 2013, IEBC has worked closely with national security agencies and other stakeholders under the Election Security Arrangement Programme (ESAP) a strategic coordination framework that has proven vital in maintaining electoral integrity and building public confidence. He lauded these partnerships, describing them as instrumental in delivering peaceful and credible elections. The Chairperson cited the 2022 Post-Election Evaluation Report, which reaffirmed the effectiveness of this collaboration, highlighting that ESAP significantly enhanced coordination between the Commission, the National Police Service, and other stakeholders. This, he noted, played a critical role in ensuring safe and peaceful elections across the country. Underscoring that election security is a continuous process, the Chairperson stressed that it spans the entire electoral cycle from voter registration, voter education, and campaigns to nominations, polling, tallying, results declaration, and even post-election activities.

title: Continuous voter registration to resume in September in preparation for 2027 GE9th Sep 2025
text: The Commission hereby announces that Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) will resume on Monday, 29th September 2025. This is in line with its constitutional mandate under Article 88(4) of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010. This exercise is a vital step in ensuring that every eligible Kenyan has the opportunity to participate in shaping the country’s future through democratic elections. It is particularly directed towards young people who have recently attained 18 years, and all citizens who have not yet registered or need to update their voter information. Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC noted that in readiness for the upcoming CVR exercise, the Commission has initiated a series of preparatory activities to ensure the process is efficient, inclusive, and transparent. These activities are critical for laying a strong foundation for a successful nationwide rollout. They include: Mapping of Registration Centres: Verifying both existing and proposed centres to ensure accessibility across the country. Stakeholder Engagements: Holding consultative forums at the constituency level to build awareness and promote participation. Geospatial Data Consolidation: Collecting constituency, county, and national-level data to guide resource planning. Preparation of Kenya Integrated Election Management System (KIEMS) Kits: Configuring and testing KIEMS kits. Gazettement of Officers: Official appointment of registration officers as required by law. Training of Registration Personnel: Equipping field officers with necessary skills for effective service delivery. Packaging and Distribution of Materials: Timely dispatch of registration materials to all operational areas. Data Protection Compliance: Conducting a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) to ensure full copliance with data protection laws. Voter Education Activities: Rolling out voter education programs to inform and engage the public. “Eligible Kenyans may register at any IEBC Constituency Office, except in areas currently with by-elections. Services available include new voter registration, transfer of voter registration to a new location, correction or update of voter details, and inspection of voter registration status,” said Ethekon.
